correctness.rationale: Every cyclic trigram multiplicity equals a run-singleton count, long-run count or run-length excess, which fixes independent zero- and one-run vector statistics. Stars-and-bars counts each ordered vector as binom(r,s)binom(T+r-s-1,r-s-1); elementary binomial inequalities give 1, r or >r possibilities, with 1 exactly U and r exactly D. Diagonal cyclic shifting of r paired run positions yields one orbit precisely for U/U,U/D,D/U. Summing run-total weights gives the stated rational generating function and asymptotic 8n/3 + O(1). Actual standalone verify.py checks 1,048,574 words, 58,833 necklaces, full singleton classifications n<=19, and 120 rational coefficients. Infinite proof is independent of finite enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: There are broader algorithms for deciding whether one observed reconstruction is unique, but a general decision procedure does not itself give the explicit necessary/sufficient run-type classification, the all-length generating function or its linear asymptotic. The labeled-edge Eulerian uniqueness theorem tests a stronger and often false condition when parallel occurrences are indistinguishable, so it does not subsume this exact string-fibre classification.

value.rationale: A complete description of the uniquely reconstructible unrestricted binary circles from the smallest nontrivial fixed k-mer histogram has direct structural interest in cyclic short-read assembly. The theorem separates two simple one-run types from irreducible ambiguity, handles periodic words, gives an exact rational all-length census and proves linear growth against a much larger space of feasible profiles. These are natural mathematical objects and the result is not a renaming or a bounded census.
